files.name: m_apb_if.sv
m_tlul_if.sv
m_apb_tlul_bridge.sv

open_points: Section 8 / REQ-PARAM-001 (BR-3-33, BR-4-02, BR-8-09): the elaboration-time report of illegal parameter values is NOT in the RTL. RTL_RULES RR-11 forbids $fatal/$error, and the approved decision places the check in the verification source set (one elaboration-time $fatal per illegal value). The RTL itself does not clamp values.

Section 8 (BR-8-03): PARA_SRC_ID is declared as a 32-bit parameter (style of the section 8 example). Only bits [PARA_SRC_W-1:0] are used, through the localparam LPARA_SRC_ID. A value that does not fit is truncated in the RTL and must be caught by the verification-set elaboration check.

Sections 5.4 and 10.1: m_tlul_if loads channel A only when w_req_launch=1 AND the TL-UL FSM is in ENUM_ST_IDLE (w_a_load). By the invariant 'TL-UL FSM idle whenever APB FSM idle' the extra condition is always true, so behaviour is unchanged. It was added as a conservative guard so a second request can never overwrite an outstanding one.

Section 5.1 / 10.1: reg_a_valid is kept as a separate flop, as the spec requires. It is redundant with TL-UL state ENUM_ST_REQ: it is set on the same edge as the REQ entry and cleared on the same acceptance edge.

Section 10.1 / DEC-009: outside a completion, reg_prdata holds its last value. reg_pready and reg_pslverr are cleared on every edge that is not a completion edge, which includes the edge that leaves ENUM_ST_DONE.

Section 10.1: the 2-bit FSMs leave encoding 2'b11 unused (APB FSM) and 2'b11 unused (TL-UL FSM). Both recover to ENUM_ST_IDLE through the default branch. The response flops are not otherwise affected in that case.

REQ-IF-004 / ASM-001 (BR-3-18, BR-20-01): o_apb_pready is high for exactly one cycle per transfer and only in ENUM_ST_DONE. That cycle is an Access cycle only if the Requester follows REF-001. The bridge does not look at PSEL/PENABLE outside the Setup check. A transfer that starts with PENABLE=1 is never answered (accepted limitation).
DEC-003 / ERR-006 (BR-12-09, BR-20-07): there is no timeout. A device that never responds keeps the APB FSM in ENUM_ST_BUSY until reset.

Sections 6.2 / 14.3: the unused inputs i_apb_pprot, i_tlul_d_param, i_tlul_d_size, i_tlul_d_sink and i_tlul_d_user are not routed into the submodules. They are waived in the top with 'verilator lint_off UNUSED' plus a WAIVER comment. The UNUSED group name was used rather than UNUSEDSIGNAL so the waiver works with both older and newer Verilator releases.
Section 14.1 (default_nettype none checking): each file starts with `default_nettype none and ends with `default_nettype wire, so the setting does not leak into other compilation units.

Section 5.1: the internal-interface ports of the submodules are named o_req_*/i_resp_* (m_apb_if) and i_req_*/o_resp_* (m_tlul_if), following the i_/o_ prefix rule. In the top they are connected through the wires w_req_launch, w_req_wr, w_req_addr, w_req_wdata, w_resp_valid, w_resp_err and w_resp_rdata of section 5.1 (w_resp_valid is w_resp_hit inside m_tlul_if). These module outputs are combinational by design; REQ-IF-003 applies to the top-level ports only.

REQ-VER-001, section 15 and BR-15.* rules (protocol checkers, SVA, coverage, scoreboard, sticky error counters) are verification-source-set items. They are not implementable in the synthesizable RTL and are not included.
notes: The RTL is three files: m_apb_if (APB side), m_tlul_if (TL-UL side) and m_apb_tlul_bridge (structural top). Every flop has an asynchronous active-low reset to 0. Every output that changes comes from a flop; the constant fields are tie-offs (DEC-005). Setup is detected by level only. The design was checked by reading; no tool was run here.
